title: Florentine family letter of March 1443/1447 with short runs of digit-like cipher (3, z, 8, 7, g, t) among clear news, bare
correspondents: unsigned family letter (names Benedetto, the Tornabuoni, Albertaccio, Ricciardo; Medici circle) -> "Ricciardo"? (addressee on verso not read)

shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo avanti il Principato, filza CXXXVII, doc. 40 (pencil 49, old 23)
folio_note: One leaf, recto: about 20 lines of clear family news; at least four short cipher runs written in the same hand with the same dot-separated layout: line 11 end ("... tu no(n) [3 signs] z3z3z4z3"), line 13 ("g3ttz1. 93 z3z3z4z3"), line 14 ("a z3z4z3z3z#z3. 83z3. gttztt"), and a group at the end of line 18; signs are a small set of digit-like forms (3, z, 8, 7, 4) and g/t letters, repeating like a vowel-and-number cipher. title: Bernardo Dovizi da Bibbiena from the royal camp in Romagna, 4 October 1494: long clear letter with names spelled in a sign cipher (three groups, one of about 20 signs), bare; Piero de' Medici's glossed letter of 28 October in the same signs
correspondents: Bernardo Dovizi da Bibbiena ("B. ... Bib.") -> Piero di Lorenzo de' Medici
place: camp of the duke of Calabria, Romagna
language: Italian (clear with sign-cipher names: x o u u + 8 π, x o u x o)
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo avanti il Principato, filza LXXII, doc. 77 (cc. 83-88)
folio_note: Six sides of clear narrative (a "facto venereo" at the camp, Cesena); a name group "x o u u + 8 π" recurs (c. 84r-v, 86v), a second group "x o u x o" recurs about ten times (cc. 86v-88v), and a lady's name is given in about 20 signs on c. 84v ("una nobilissima et bellissima Madonna chiamata ..."). Address c. 83v.
status: Bare (1272 px on c. 84v; contact sheet and 800 px elsewhere). The sign set (x, ÷, π, u, h, 8, 3, +, 11) is the one glossed in LXXII 81 (Piero de' Medici, Pietrasanta 28 Oct 1494, to ser Piero da Bibbiena), so the names should read directly. Moncallero's Epistolario di Bernardo Dovizi da Bibbiena (1955) prints his letters of 1490-94; whether this one and its names are deciphered there was not checked.
why: Small (three names) but readable at once from LXXII 81; low value except as a key check.
verify: Read the groups with the LXXII 81 glosses; check Moncallero 1955 for the letter of 4 Oct 1494.

title: Antonio Maria Bonanni of San Gimignano, Piacenza, 1512-13: two letters to ser Giovanni da Poppi with cipher runs (letters and digits with superscript index figures), bare
correspondents: Antonio Maria Bonanni (Bonannius geminianensis), Piacenza -> ser Giovanni da Poppi, Medici secretary
language: Italian (cipher runs: Latin letters and digits with superscript figures 1-4)
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo avanti il Principato, filza LXXII, docs. 130 and 140
folio_note: 130r ("Placentie die vij Martij XII", signed "Anto: maria Bonannus Gem."): five lines with four runs of 10-30 symbols (e.g. "P4 5T8 Z584 3 5 X y d 6 3 d"), small figures 1-4 written above many symbols; 140r (Piacenza 6 June [1513]): about 2 lines (45 symbols) of the same kind. Versos: address "S. Iohanni de Puppio secretario Florentie".
status: Bare (1228 px on 130, 800 px on 140): the superscript figures are index marks (homophone numbers), not a gloss. The same superscript-figure style is used in Acciaiuoli's 1513 cipher (LXXII 190-192) and Pandolfini's 1514-15 cipher (row below).
why: A Medici agent in Lombardy in the year of the Medici restoration; short, but the superscript-index system ties it to the better-keyed 1513-15 Medici ciphers.
verify: Transcribe both; test the Acciaiuoli 190/191 table and the Pandolfini table; look at doc. 139 (5 June 1513).

title: Francesco Pandolfini, Florentine orator in France, 1514-15: seven cipher letters with no decipherment identified, beside about twelve cipher/decipherment pairs of the same system in MAP LXXII
correspondents: Francesco Pandolfini, orator at the French court -> the Otto di Pratica / Lorenzo de' Medici (duke of Urbino)
language: Italian (letter/digit cipher with superscript figures, between clear passages)
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo avanti il Principato, filza LXXII, docs. 297, 307, 309, 310, 311, 322, 333
folio_note: 297 (copy, Paris 22? Jan 1514 st. fior.): 8 cipher lines; 307 (c. 369, Feb 1514 st. fior.): almost a page; 309 (c. 378, to Lorenzo, 26? Feb): 10 lines; 310 (cc. 380-381, 25 Feb-2 Mar): about 70 cipher lines in blocks; 311 (c. 382): nearly two sides; 322 (copy of two chapters to Rome, Oct 1514): two 9-line blocks; 333 (c. 417, to Lorenzo, 27 Dec MDXIII or MDXIIII, read both ways): 3-5 lines.
status: No gloss on these pages (contact sheet and 800 px), and the paging matched none of them with a filed clear text; some may be covered by the unheaded clear copies 284, 306, 316, 332, 337, 344, 347, 350, 365-366 and 419 (not aligned). Pairs in the filza: 281/285, 287/288, 290/291-292, 293/335, 308 (glossed)/313, 315/316, 317/348, 320/321, 330/331, 334/332, 338/339, 340/341, 342/343, 346/345, 349/348; glossed 318, 319; decipherments 368 ("Decifrato ... a Lorenzo"), 366 ("tratti di cifra"). The first pass recorded 215 (1514, interlinear) as the key text of this system.
why: A full key can be rebuilt from the pairs, and the seven letters read; the embassy covers Louis XII's last months, Francis I's accession and the run-up to Marignano.
verify: Align 287 with 288 and 342 with 343 to rebuild the table (superscripts as homophone marks); read the seven; check each against the unheaded clear copies first.
